jobs.description:
**A Snapshot of Your Day

**Join Siemens Energy as a Product Manager with a strong focus on Wind Power and SCADA systems, where you act as the key link between business needs and agile development teams. Ideally, you have knowledge from the energy sector - maybe you even have a hands-on understanding of how wind farm operators work and the daily challenges they face, translating this into scalable and maintainable digital solutions. You operate across both strategic and operational levels – shaping product direction while working closely with teams to ensure efficient delivery. Your soft skills are strong and you know how to navigate having many different stakeholders in a dynamic environment, as well as manage both upwards, sideways and downwards. You are the type of person that takes ownership, and with a pragmatic mindset, you balance innovation, cost awareness, and technical feasibility to deliver competitive solutions that create real business value.

**How You'll Make An Impact

**

• Act as Product Manager for OT software and SCADA-related solutions, owning prioritization and value delivery across agile teams

• Translate real-world wind farm operational challenges into product requirements, ensuring solutions are practical and customer-focused

• Balance strategic roadmap ownership with hands-on involvement in agile delivery teams

• Drive prioritization based on business value, cost efficiency, and technical feasibility

• Identify technology trends and partnerships that support scalable, maintainable, and competitive solutions

**What You Bring

**

• Master’s degree in software engineering or similar combined with strong experience in Wind Power SCADA systems and OT environments

• Hands-on understanding of wind farm operations and the challenges faced by operators and service organizations

• Proven experience working both strategically and operationally within Product Management or similar roles

• Strong business mindset with focus on cost efficiency, maintainability, and pragmatic decision-making

• Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills across technical and business domains

**Who is Siemens Energy?

**At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With +100,000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation. Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemensenergy.com/employeevideo

**Our Commitment to Diversity

**Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity, we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences.

**Rewards/Benefits

**

• Become a part of our mission for sustainability: Clean energy for generations to come

• A global team of diverse colleagues who share passion for renewable energy

• Personal and professional development to grow internally within our organization

• Flexible working hours as well as home-office

• Attractive remuneration package (fixed/variable)

• Local benefits such as subsidized lunch and public transport tickets, employee discounts and much more

YOUR NEXT HR CHALLENGE STARTS HERE

Do you know HR operations, and want to be a part of continuously optimizing our processes ?

We are looking for a People Services & Country Advisor to join our team in Kolding. You will combine hands-on HR expertise with knowledge of Danish employment legislation, and be working where local requirements, people and global HR processes meet.

People Services provides standardized services across the Vattenfall Group, and in this role, you will help ensure they work effectively in a Danish context.

What you will do

• Provide practical HR advice and guidance to employees, managers and HR colleagues

• Prepare contracts, amendments and other employment documentation

• Support payroll, time registration, pension and benefits processes

• Ensure high-quality employee data and work with SAP, SuccessFactors and ServiceNow

• Improve HR processes and identify opportunities for simplification, digitalization and automation

• Collaborate with colleagues across Denmark and our international People organization

• Develop and deliver relevant HR training to employees, managers and HR Business Partners

Qualifications

Is this you?

You have solid experience within HR Operations or a similar environment, together with good knowledge of Danish employment legislation. You enjoy solving problems, taking ownership, and turning complex HR questions into practical solutions.

You communicate confidently in Danish and English and are comfortable working across teams, functions and countries at all levels of the organization.

Experience with SAP, SuccessFactors or ServiceNow is an advantage.

An interest in, or experience using AI as a practical tool to simplify and improve HR processes would be a strong advantage.

Experience working with blue-collar employees and Danish trade unions is a preferred competence.

You will not be expected to know everything. But we do expect you to be curious enough to find out.

Most importantly, you bring drive, curiosity and the confidence to challenge how things are done and help us make them better.

Why join us?

You will join a team built on trust and honesty, where we speak up, challenge each other constructively, support one another, and, importantly, laugh a lot.

You will have real ownership, an international network and the opportunity to influence how HR services are developed in Denmark. The role also offers a hybrid working arrangement, with the possibility of working from home up to two days per week.

If you enjoy solving HR challenges, making complicated things simpler and shaping how People Services should work tomorrow, we would love to hear from you.

Additional Information

Location:

Kolding

At Vattenfall we are convinced that diversity contributes to build a more profitable and attractive company and we strive to be good role model regarding diversity. Vattenfall works actively for all employees to have the same opportunities and rights regardless of gender, ethnicity, age, transgender identity or expression, religion or other belief, disability or sexual orientation.

Since Vattenfall is a part of critical infrastructure in multiple countries, many of our services are security classed.

If this position is security classified the final candidate might be subject to a security vetting/clearance process according to national legislation

How to apply

We welcome your application in English, including CV via the link, no later than the 13th of November 2026.

We encourage you to apply as soon as possible, as applications will be reviewed and interviews conducted on an ongoing basis.

If you have questions regarding the position, you are welcome to contact Manager Vibeke Medum, People Services & Country Advisor DK, on vibeke.medum@vattenfall.com

We look forward to receiving your application!

Energy is our contribution to quality of life – day after day. With around 21,000 colleagues Vattenfall provides comprehensive electricity and heating offerings to several million customers in northern Europe. For the work ahead we need people who are fully dedicated to our customers and to a sustainable society – people like you.

Company Description

Vattenfall is a leading European energy company driving the transition to a sustainable energy system. We have been electrifying industries, powering homes and transforming life through innovation for more than 100 years. We employ around 21 000 people mostly in our core markets in Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, and the UK.

Business Area Wind is responsible for Vattenfall’s Onshore and Offshore Wind as well as other renewable activities such as solar PV and batteries. We develop, construct and operate wind generation and we have a clear strategy to develop our solar PV and battery operations further.

At Aalborg University, The Technical Faculty of IT and Design, Department of Architecture, Design and Media Technology (Copenhagen Campus) a full-time position as Postdoc is available for a period of 2 years from February 1, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The Department of Architecture, Design, and Media Technology has as its goal the development of an innovative cluster of engineering-based environments for education and research which integrate creativity, engineering and technology within the disciplines of architecture, urban design, industrial design, lighting design, digital design and interactive media. The department is a leading research and educational environment in Denmark that addresses the challenge of the interplay between creativity and technology and develops new areas in research and education directed towards the end-user.

Your work tasks    The successful candidate will contribute to research, supervision, teaching, and semester coordination within Lighting Design at the Department of Architecture, Design and Media Technology, Aalborg University, Copenhagen.

Research activities will be conducted with the transdisciplinary Lighting Design Lab and will primarily contribute to externally funded research projects addressing societal challenges through lighting design, technology, and human-centric approaches.

Supervision responsibilities will primarily be associated with the MSc program in Lighting Design, which includes approximately 60 international students. Students work in project groups on semester-based lighting design projects and individually or in groups on master theses. The projects are grounded in a strong understanding of design-research processes and integrate theories, methods, and approaches across relevant academic disciplines. The position will also include coordination of semesters and related educational activities.

Teaching will primarily focus on the engineering and technical aspects of lighting design, particularly within courses such as Lighting Fundamentals and Evidence-Based Lighting Design. Topics include fundamental photometric and colorimetric concepts, lighting laws and principles, measurement quantities and methods, international standards, and objective methods for the measurement, observation, analysis, and evaluation of lighting conditions.

**Your competencies

**The successful candidate is expected to demonstrate the ability to identify emerging societal challenges and translate them into future competence and skill requirements for the lighting design profession. The candidate should also demonstrate an understanding of how these competences and skills can be integrated into teaching and research in lighting design at the highest academic level.

The candidate should demonstrate the ability to attract external research funding and to lead or contribute to interdisciplinary research projects involving multiple partners and stakeholders. Experience with innovation and cross-sector collaboration between academia, industry, and public-sector organizations is considered particularly relevant.

The candidate must have experience in relevant teaching and supervising diverse student groups, with a focus on developing an understanding of transdisciplinary design processes supported by relevant technical skills and a strong scientific foundation.

The candidate must demonstrate strong collaborative skills and the ability to work effectively as part of an international and interdisciplinary team of lighting designers, architects, engineers, and other researchers within the Lighting Design Lab in Copenhagen.

Who we are

The Lighting Design Lab brings together lighting designers, engineers, architects, and researchers who work collaboratively to advance teaching and research in lighting design. The Lab supports a two-year international MSc programme in Lighting Design and a strong transdisciplinary research environment.

Our work integrates architecture, engineering, AI, and media technology and is often conducted in collaboration with private-sector partners to address relevant societal challenges. Research and experimental activities combine contextual and architectural analysis of the light environment, including daylight and electric lighting, with consideration of human visual and non-visual needs and dynamic lighting conditions.

Design solutions are based on a perceived understanding of light environments supported by advanced technologies such as lighting control, sensing systems, sky scanners, and smartphone-based applications, while remaining grounded in human and societal needs. The Lab also maintains a strong international network and collaborates with leading universities and research environments within lighting design.

You may read more about the department here: https://www.create.aau.dk/om-create

Qualification requirements Appointment as postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level.

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma)

• List of publications, with an indication of the attached publications that you wish to be taken into account in the assessment. You may attach a maximum of five publications.

• Documentation of teaching qualifications if relevant.

• Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc.

• Additional qualifications in relation to the position

• References/recommendations

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. International staff are encouraged, with support from the university, to learn Danish during their employment in order to support their integration into the workplace and Danish society.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact associate professor Ellen Kathrine Hansen, ekh@create.aau.dk Phone: 0045 21723181

Further information

Read more about our recruitment process here

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Salary and terms of employment  The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Postdoc”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

About Userlink

Userlink runs AI agents in production at several hundred Nordic webshops, including Bahne, XL-BYG, Coolshop and Bygma. The agents handle the customer dialogue before and after the purchase, and every conversation ends up as structured data on demand and purchase barriers. The team is based in Odense.

The product and the direction

Today we sell chat. Email is rolling out now, and phone and social follow. On top of that we are building the brain: a system that brings together every signal about a webshop and its customers, understands why people buy, and why they do not, and acts on it while the buyer is still on the page. The effect is measured against a control group, so the shop can see what it means for revenue.

That moves the sale from a customer service tool to a conversation about growth, and revenue per customer can become several times what it is today.

The role

Ownership of the entire go-to-market in one place: lead generation, new business, partners and existing customers. You run the process from first contact to signature, find out what works and write the sales process the rest of the company will follow.

Lead generation is yours as a minimum. You own where the meetings come from: the customer profile, the lead lists and the sourcing of the right webshops, outbound and the campaigns that have to fill the pipeline. You measure what a meeting costs to acquire and which channels carry, and you shut down the ones that do not. You build it yourself at first and set direction for marketing and meeting booking as they come on board.

The partner channel has to be built. Agencies and platform partners need to be found, judged realistically and sold alongside until they can do it on their own.

Growth in the existing customer base is part of it, especially as email, phone and the brain roll out, measured against clear monthly and quarterly targets.

Price, pitch, customer profile and process are yours. They change when they do not work, and the team is built as the numbers allow. Denmark is home turf, but we already have customers and partners in DACH and the Netherlands, and those markets grow from here.

Decisions are made on arguments, not titles. Ideas get challenged regardless of where they come from, and the best one wins.

Why founding

You do not step into a finished sales organisation. You build the commercial side together with the founder, and what you decide on price, pitch, process and the first hires is what Userlink will sell on for years.

That is why the role comes with equity. You help build the company, and you own part of what you build. In return we expect you to take responsibility like a co-owner, also when things are unclear or go wrong.

Profile

• Has built sales in a B2B SaaS company as one of the first salespeople, with own meetings and own closes

• Has built lead generation from scratch, through outbound, partners or marketing, and knows what pipeline costs to acquire

• Has had a budget and hit it, and can explain in detail how

• Sells personally and teaches others to do it at the same time

• Experience selling outside Denmark, and a feel for what changes when you do

• Strong product and technology understanding, and uses AI every day in their own work

• Danish at native level, confident on calls, in meetings and in demos

• Fluent English is mandatory. English is the office language at Userlink

The person

• Dreams of owning and building a company

• Ideally has tried starting something and knows what it takes

• Thinks like a founder, not an employee

• Happily gives more than a regular job asks for, because it is fun

• Says things as they are, and can take the same in return

• Takes ownership and looks for solutions rather than excuses

• Curious, learns fast and has a positive mindset

What we offer

• Competitive salary plus uncapped commission

• Equity

• Short decision paths and close collaboration with product and engineering

• Office at Storms Pakhus in Odense, where we are every day

Application process

We take the time it takes to find the right match.

• Introductory conversation

• Conversation about expectations and terms

Write to jobs@userlink.ai about a SaaS product you helped scale, where the meetings came from, and what you personally did to make it happen.

jobs.occupation: Technical Lead - Substation Automation and Communication Systems
jobs.description:
Do you have experience with automation and communication systems for high-voltage substations? Can you lead technical work packages and coordinate specialist contributions to deliver an integrated solution? Join COWI as our new Technical Lead and contribute to the development of Denmark’s electricity transmission infrastructure.

Take technical responsibility for substation automation projects

We are looking for an experienced engineer to take technical responsibility for substation automation and communication systems in high-voltage substation projects. You will work on projects ranging from new substations to extensions, refurbishment and replacement of systems at existing sites. You will coordinate specialist contributions, manage technical interfaces and ensure that individual work packages meet the requirements of the overall substation automation solution.

The role combines technical expertise with responsibility for coordinating engineering activities, monitoring progress and ensuring the quality of technical deliverables. You will work closely with the project manager, technical specialists and other engineering disciplines throughout project execution.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Lead and coordinate the technical delivery of substation automation and communication systems.

• Plan and follow up on engineering activities, technical deliverables and milestones within your scope.

• Coordinate specialist contributions and ensure consistency across technical work packages.

• Ensure that technical solutions and documentation comply with project requirements, customer specifications and applicable standards.

• Manage technical interfaces between automation, communication systems, protection systems, primary equipment and auxiliary systems.

• Identify and resolve technical issues in collaboration with specialists and other engineering disciplines.

• Participate in project meetings and advise the project manager on technical matters, dependencies and risks within your area of responsibility.

• Coordinate technical activities with customers, suppliers and other project stakeholders.

Your expertise

You combine a strong technical foundation with a structured approach to planning and coordination. You can assess how individual systems and specialist contributions fit together, communicate technical requirements clearly and follow through on agreed actions.

You work independently and build effective working relationships with colleagues, customers and project partners.

You will also bring:

• A degree in electrical engineering or an equivalent technical qualification, together with more than five years of relevant experience in automation for high-voltage substations.

• A solid understanding of substation automation systems, including control and monitoring functions, communication networks and interfaces to protection equipment.

• An understanding of how substation secondary systems interface with high-voltage primary equipment.

• Experience coordinating technical work packages, planning engineering activities and following up on specialist deliverables.

• The ability to assess technical solutions, manage interfaces and maintain an overview of quality, progress and dependencies.

• Professional proficiency in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

• The ability to obtain the required security clearance and fulfil the requirements for the designated on-site role of “holdleder” at high-voltage substations.

Your place of work

Depending on project requirements, you may work from one of COWI’s offices in Denmark, at Energinet project locations or partly from home. Travel within Denmark is expected.

A place to work and so much more

At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers.

We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home.

With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

Got more questions?

If you have any unanswered questions about the role or what we have to offer, please reach out to Head of Discipline Carsten Sass Husum at CSHU@COWI.COM.

Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

Before you apply

All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture.

Equal opportunity employer

COWI provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability or genetics. In addition to federal law requirements, COWI complies with applicable state and local laws governing non-discrimination in employment in every location in which the company has facilities. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

**Account Executive - Denmark

**Aarhus | Copenhagen

About Puzzel 🔍

We're the AI-native customer experience platform built in Norway, trusted across Europe, and growing fast. For 25 years we've helped contact centres deliver faster, more human service — without the clutter or complexity. Today we're #1 in the Nordics, scaling rapidly in the UK and the Netherlands, with one ambition: become Europe's clear CX market leader.

Puzzel Values 🎯

• 
Built on Trust - our Nordic foundation. Customers, partners, and each other.

• 
Stronger Together - one team, one purpose, shared wins.

• 
Stay Hungry - we raise our game every day.

Why we’re proud**🏆**

• 
Frost Radar Innovation & Growth Leader in EMEA Customer Experience Platforms (2025)

• 
CX Awards 'Best Mid-Market Contact Center Platform' (2024)

• 
Flexa Top 10 most inclusive companies and Top 25 for work-life balance, diversity and inclusion, pet-friendly companies and professional services (2026)

• 
Consistently high Glassdoor rating

• 
Mercer-benchmarked pay for equity and market fairness

• 
Puzzel doesn't just build AI for our customers — we’ve embraced it internally, adopting it across the business to work smarter and faster

Read more about us here.

What you'll do 🏡💻

This is a 100% net-new business role. You’ll drive your own prospecting, while working closely with our SDR, our partners and our marketing team to create and convert opportunities. Our SDR focuses on our top 100 accounts every day, marketing supports you with lead generation and events, and partners are an important source of new ARR in Denmark.

You’re proactive, solution-oriented and not afraid to shake things up. You communicate excellently, manage your own time and processes well, and know how to close deals.

You should have good time management skills, be comfortable running your own processes and excel at the following:

• 
Building and nurturing relationships with customers and partners or creating business opportunities from scratch - it's important to highlight that you'll be managing the full sales cycle from initial prospecting to close.

• 
Generate your own pipeline through outbound activity, spending a meaningful part of each week on direct and partner-led prospecting

• 
Collaborate with the SDR and marketing to turn target accounts, leads and events into qualified opportunities

• 
Recruit, enable and co-sell with partners and channel organisations to generate and close pipeline

• 
Run discovery calls, demos and presentations, building a thorough understanding of each customer’s needs, business and processes

• 
Take performance and budget responsibility for your own portfolio, driving growth and profitability

• 
Use our systems and automated sequences (Salesforce and Outreach in particular) to minimise manual work and follow RevOps best practice

The must haves 💪

• 
Danish native level speaker + strong English

• 
Technological understanding and interest in the field of cloud-based services

• 
At least 3 years’ experience managing full sales cycle, from prospect to close

• 
Proven outbound experience, and a track record of generating your own pipeline (ideally you still do your own outreach today)

• 
CX or complex B2B SaaS sales experience

• 
Experience working with structured sales methodologies (MEDDPICC and/or Challenger preferable) & sales pipelining

• 
Proactive, entrepreneurial mentality and willingness to self-generate pipeline are a must

• 
Autonomy and confidence to sell into a growing market

• 
The nice to haves ➕➕➕

• 
Experience of selling through partners or channels

• 
Exposure to an international environment

• 
Additional language skills

• 
CCaaS / competitor industry experience

The location

This role is based in our Aarhus or Copenhagen offices, with a hybrid set up of 2-3 days per week in the office.

What to expect from the interview process ❔

• 
Screening call with Talent Acquisition

• 
1st interview with the Sales Director & local Account Executive

• 
Final panel presentation

Diversity & Inclusion 🌍

We want everyone at Puzzel to feel able to be their true, authentic self at work – regardless of nationality, race, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, physical ability, age or economic background.

We're proud of our diverse, global workforce, but there's more to do. Our current gender split is 25% female to 75% male – in line with the SaaS average, but not where we want to be. Here's how we're improving it:

• 
Our C-suite has moved from 100% male in 2023 to a 5:3 male-to-female split today.

• 
Female hires grew from 23.6% in 2021 to 41% in 2024, dipping to 34% in 2025 — a trend we watch closely, but never treating as a tick-box exercise.

• 
We partner with Flexa, to compound our aspiration to attract a diverse talent pool.

• 
We work with state employment initiatives in Norway and Sweden on internship and apprenticeship routes, to help early-years talent into the workforce.

One Last Thing ☝🏻

Even if you're only a 75% match for this role, we still want to hear from you — this list is indicative, and skills can always be learnt.

We're unable to offer sponsorship for this role, so you'll need existing eligibility to work in the country you're applying to.

By applying you accept the terms of our Data & Privacy notice.

**About The Role

**As a Senior Observability Engineer at Saxo, you will join a specialised team responsible for the bank's observability platforms. We build and continuously improve solutions that provide visibility into the performance, stability, and health of critical business systems across our hybrid infrastructure.

You will help shape the future of Saxo's observability landscape by designing and operating solutions for metrics, logs, traces, and events across cloud and on-premises environments. Your work will enable engineering teams to better understand, monitor, and improve the systems that power Saxo.

**Team perspective

**_"We are the eyes and ears of Saxo Bank's platform health. Our work is critical to maintaining stable and continuous operations across the organisation.

__Our team is based in Denmark and India and consists of five specialists. While supporting our current platforms, we are also executing our roadmap for the next generation of observability capabilities."

_**Responsibilities

**

• Own and support the day-to-day operation of Saxo's observability platform.

• Partner closely with engineering teams to deliver meaningful monitoring and visibility across business-critical systems.

• Drive priorities, technical direction, and platform improvements within the team.

• Act as the observability platform architect, ensuring scalability, reliability, and long-term maintainability.

• Play a key role in delivering the next generation of Saxo's observability platform in collaboration with Enterprise Architecture, platform teams, and business stakeholders.

**What Success Looks Like

**

• Build expertise across our observability ecosystem, including Elastic, Grafana, Kibana, Kubernetes, SCOM, and Windows Server.

• Improve visibility, reliability, and operational efficiency by reducing alert noise, enhancing dashboards, and driving actionable insights.

• Define and promote standards for logging, metrics, dashboards, and alerting.

• Collaborate with engineering, platform, and security teams to ensure observability is embedded across solutions.

• Lead incident investigations, contribute to post-mortems, and turn lessons learned into platform improvements.

• Optimise platform performance, scalability, and cost.

• Share knowledge through documentation, best practices, and technical guidance across the organisation.

**Your profile

**You have 5+ years of experience in Software Engineering, Site Reliability Engineering, DevOps, Platform Engineering, or a similar role, with a strong focus on observability.

**You Bring Hands-on Experience With Observability Technologies Such As

**

• Metrics: Prometheus, Grafana, CloudWatch, Datadog, Dynatrace, New Relic, or similar.

• Logging: Elastic Stack, Splunk, Loki, Cloud Logging, or similar.

• Tracing: OpenTelemetry, Jaeger, Zipkin, X-Ray, or equivalent tracing solutions.

**You Also Have Experience With

**

• SRE practices, including SLOs, SLIs, error budgets, and incident management.

• Distributed systems and cloud-native architectures.

• Operating and optimising Elastic Stack in production environments.

• Grafana and Kibana for dashboarding, visualisation, and alerting.

• Windows Server administration and monitoring, ideally including SCOM.

• Public cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.

• Kubernetes, Docker, and container-based environments.

• Infrastructure-as-Code and CI/CD tooling (Terraform, Helm, CloudFormation, Pulumi, GitOps, etc.).

• Scripting or development experience in languages such as Java, Python, or Node.js.

**We get curious people invested in the world

**When you work at Saxo, you become a Saxonian and part of a purpose-driven organisation, where good ideas are always taken seriously, and where you can make a true impact. We are invested in your development, and you can expect a robust career from day one when you join Saxo – no matter which role you take on.

You will join 2,500 other ambitious colleagues across 11 countries and become part of an international organisation. Working in Saxo, you will get to meet colleagues from many different cultures and backgrounds, and you should know that we value diversity and inclusion and see it as a genuine source of strength to drive growth, foster innovation and position us for long-term success.

We encourage an open feedback culture and supportive team environments enabling employees to grow and fulfil their career aspirations.

When you bring passion, curiosity, drive and team spirit, your learning journey will be dynamic and your career opportunities in Saxo will be immense.

At Saxo we don’t just offer a job – we offer an opportunity to invest in your future!

Senior Gameplay Programmer on WHAT THE CAR?

Do you love working in small, creative teams turning wild ideas into a reality? What about having creative and technical ownership from ideation through to release? Read on!

Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by a simple mission: to make everyone laugh.

WHAT THE CAR? is our absurdly silly racing adventure game which addresses fundamental questions such as… What if a car had legs? Or a jetpack? Or secretly identified as a sailboat? First launched in 2023 on Apple Arcade and now also on Steam, it has gained a steady following of dedicated fans who have contributed hundreds of thousands of community-built levels.

We’re looking for a Senior Gameplay Programmer to help us continue to build upon CAR’s success by expanding upon its absurdly silly universe! We believe the best people to come up with ideas are the ones implementing them, so we expect a high degree of creativity and game design knowledge from our Gameplay Programmers, in addition to their crazy tech skills. This role involves around 60% programming and 40% game design.

Here’s what that looks like day to day

• 
Build and ship gameplay code. You’ll implement features end-to-end in an existing Unity/C# codebase and ship regularly in a live environment.

• 
Generate design ideas. You’ll take part in shaping features, articulate intent, evaluate tradeoffs, and iterate through discussion with the team.

• 
Keep the game healthy. Fix bugs, improve systems, review test videos, and document findings so issues don’t come back to haunt us.

• 
Extend and refine what’s there. You’ll build on existing mechanics, making them more robust and enjoyable for players.

• 
Support and collaborate. You’re part of a small, closely knit, cross discipline team where people help each other reach their goals.

• 
Prototype and let go. Not everything ships, and that’s fine. Comfort with iteration and refactoring is part of the job.

You’re a great match if

• 
You have 8+ years of commercial game development experience, having shipped at least two games as part of a team

• 
You have strong Unity and C# skills. You’re comfortable navigating a shared codebase and writing maintainable code you’d be proud to hand off

• 
You care about stability, performance, and long-term maintainability, and you leave systems better than you found them

• 
You genuinely value collaboration and working very closely with every member of the team

• 
You approach other people’s ideas with openness and try to understand the intention before giving feedback or pushing back

Join us as Executive Protection Advisor at Maersk

Maersk’s Protective Services function helps keep our executive leadership, their families and designated senior leaders safe, connected and able to lead the business with confidence. We do this through intelligence-led advice, structured programmes and discreet coordination across the countries where Maersk operates.

We are looking for an Executive Protection Advisor to take ownership of our Executive Protection and Event Security programmes; co-own the executive scope of our Travel Risk Management programme and the family coverage within our Expat and Family Security Programme; and act as a trusted advisor to senior executives across Maersk and A.P. Moller Holding, as well as designated family members.

This role is for someone who leads through structure and judgement rather than visibility. You can balance operational delivery with programme development, build trust with senior stakeholders, and translate exposure into proportionate, discreet and workable solutions.

The role in brief

The Executive Protection Advisor is the trusted operational and advisory point of contact for our executive population and their closest support functions. The role sits at the centre of a global Protective Services team and works directly with the Head of Protective Services.

Approximately 60% of the role is operational. You will advise on executive travel, events, residences and family security situations; manage incidents and threats when they arise; and coordinate with Regional Heads of Security, vendors and authorities to ensure the right support is in the right place at the right time.

The remaining 40% is strategic. You will own and continuously develop the Executive Protection Programme and the Event Security Programme. You will also co-own the executive scope of Travel Risk Management and the coverage for families of Maersk’s executive leadership within our Expat and Family Security Programme, while contributing to the continued professional maturity of the function.

International travel is part of the role, including support for events, oversight of site visits, and the development and maintenance of vendor relationships. The role is based in Copenhagen.

What you will do

Programme ownership and development

·  Own the Executive Protection Programme (EPP), including its appendices, procedures and workflows, and ensure it remains current and operationally usable.

·  Own the Event Security Programme (ESP), including triggers, templates, planning standards and governance.

·  Co-own the executive travel scope of our Travel Risk Management programme and the family coverage within our Expat and Family Security Programme.

·  Prepare decision-ready executive briefings for leadership review and approval.

Executive, family and residential advisory

·  Act as the trusted contact for senior executives and designated family members on protective services matters.

·  Conduct individual exposure assessments and translate findings into proportionate, discreet, and practical measures.

·  Coordinate residential security across alarms, access control, surveillance, physical improvements and vendor delivery.

Executive travel and event coordination

·  Coordinate protective services for senior executive travel.

·  Plan and oversee event security for leadership events, off-sites and public engagements.

·  Coordinate with Regional Heads of Security, local offices, vendors and authorities to ensure consistent delivery.

Incident, threat and harassment case management

·  Lead the initial assessment of threats, harassment or incidents affecting executives, family members, or company locations.

·  Coordinate with Global Threat Intelligence, Cyber Security, Legal, HQ Security, and relevant authorities.

·  Maintain clear documentation, follow-up actions, and After-Action Reviews.

Intelligence, vendors and authorities

·  Define Protective Services’ intelligence requirements and coordinate with Global Threat Intelligence.

·  Support vendor evaluations, RFP processes and procurement collaboration across executive protection, residential security, event security and intelligence suppliers.

·  Build and maintain professional relationships with Danish and international police, authorities and security partners.

Training and onboarding

·  Deliver security onboarding and briefings for new members of Maersk’s executive leadership, Executive Assistants and relevant support functions.

·  Develop audience-appropriate awareness materials, briefings, and checklists.

About you

You are a trusted advisor, not a frontline operator. You bring the composure of someone who has worked closely with senior leadership, and you understand that judgement and discretion matter more than visibility in this environment.

You are structured, take ownership and follow matters through to closure. You are comfortable with ambiguity, able to bring orders to incomplete information, and confident in turning it into a workable plan.

You are proactive and anticipate what is coming. You engage early with Executive Assistants, regional partners and vendors, ensuring Protective Services remains a step ahead.

You communicate with clarity and confidence. You can turn a complex security topic into a concise, decision-ready briefing for a senior leader, and you can raise concerns respectfully but firmly when the situation requires it.

You understand that this is a people-focused role. Trust is the foundation, discretion is the standard and continuity is essential to effective delivery.

Qualifications

Required

·  Danish citizenship, as the role requires eligibility for national security clearance and professional cooperation with Danish authorities, including the Police and PET.

·  A relevant background in corporate protective services, executive protection, security risk management, intelligence, police, military or diplomatic security.

·  Documented experience of working professionally with authorities on security matters, or a demonstrated ability to build and maintain such relationships.

·  Experience in at least two of the following four core areas: executive protection; family and residential security; event security; or executive travel coordination.

·  Strong judgement and the ability to act autonomously in sensitive situations.

·  Exceptional discretion and interpersonal awareness.

·  Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

·  A valid driver’s license and the ability to travel internationally.

Preferred

·  Experience in a global corporate environment with executive stakeholders.

·  Experience developing and maintaining security programmes, procedures, or playbooks.

·  Experience coordinating with Regional Security teams across multiple geographies.

·  Working knowledge of ISO 31030 (Travel Risk Management) or similar standards.

·  Experience with vendor evaluation, procurement collaboration, and performance oversight.

·  Danish language skills.

Our vision is to unlock the potential of data privacy to empower a thriving digital ecosystem. We work with companies to create a healthy balance between data-driven business and privacy-led marketing for every size of enterprise. Our customers build trust with their users through improved transparency and control to drastically improve marketing and monetization, while achieving full privacy compliance.

Our GTM organization is at an inflection point after reaching more than €100M ARR in 2025. As we scale, our Salesforce ecosystem needs to evolve from a system of record into a true platform for growth – flexible, well-governed and built to support increasingly complex go-to-market motions. You'll be responsible for the technical architecture and long-term health of our Salesforce instance, translating ambitious business requirements into scalable, maintainable solutions.

You'll own the architecture and design standards across our Salesforce ecosystem. • Partner with RevOps and the GTM org to evaluate buy vs. build decisions and guide platform-native solutions over custom code wherever possible.

• Lead technical design reviews, identify risks or technical debt early and ensure solutions are secure, performant and compliant with data governance requirements.

• Stay at the frontier of the Salesforce ecosystem – continuously evaluate new platform capabilities (Data Cloud, Agentforce, Flow) and bring the right innovations into our architecture roadmap.

Requirements

Experience

• 5+ years of experience in Salesforce architecture, solution engineering or senior Salesforce development roles.

• Proven track record designing and scaling Salesforce architecture in a high-growth B2B SaaS environment.

Technical Skills

• Deep fluency in Salesforce architecture fundamentals: data modeling, security/sharing model, Flow, Apex, LWC, and integration patterns.

• Strong practical experience designing integrations via REST/SOAP APIs, middleware (MuleSoft, Workato or similar) and event-driven architecture.

**

Operating Skills**

Building keeps getting cheaper every quarter. What used to take a senior engineer a few weeks now takes an afternoon. The work that does not get cheaper is helping a real business absorb new technology, sequencing the rollout, and knowing when to slow down because something is starting to break under load.

At Heyra, we build operational AI: systems, workflows, and data platforms that live in production from day one. We work with companies that are moving quickly and need solutions that improve the way they operate.

We are looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer. Someone who goes into a client, understands the operation, spots where the real optimisation potential sits, and pushes it all the way through to execution with a strong engineering team behind them.

The role sits between engineering and consulting without fitting cleanly into either. You need to be technical enough to understand data and AI at a deep level. Commercial enough to spot where the business value sits. Patient enough to sit with a manager who is genuinely worried about the tool you just put in front of them. And stubborn enough to stay around once the launch excitement fades and the real adoption work begins.

Most people are strong in one of those. Some in two. Almost nobody walks in with all four. That is exactly the profile we are looking for.

What you will work on

You will embed directly with clients to understand the operation and where the real value sits. You will drive adoption by sequencing rollouts, working with the people who have to use the tool, and staying through the unglamorous part. You will translate business needs into AI solutions that actually ship. And you will learn when to push, when to slow down, and when something is starting to break under load.

You work closely with engineers, data specialists, strategists, and designers in a company where the distance from thinking to building is intentionally small.

**Requirements

**Experience with management consulting, change management, or adoption of AI solutions in production. An understanding of software development, ML or data engineering. Familiarity with AI and GenAI frameworks, possibly with some MLOps and evals exposure. Experience with cloud environments like Azure or GCP.

Coding with agents like Claude Code, Codex or Cursor. Working directly with clients and stakeholders. Owning delivery end to end, from a vague problem to a live, adopted solution.

Curiosity, taste and a builder mentality matter just as much to us as specific tools or years of experience.

Why Heyra

We believe consulting needs to be rewritten. We are building a consultancy designed for the agentic era. We design, build and operate AI products that change how enterprises work, from problem to prototype to production.

Heyra brings together people from engineering, strategy, product, startup and creative environments. We keep teams small, collaboration close and momentum high. We care deeply about craft, speed and building things that work in the real world.

**The Role

**As Genmab continues its transformation into a fully integrated global biotech company, the Head of Total Rewards will architect a future-ready, technology-enabled global rewards strategy that aligns with our purpose, growth ambitions, and values.

This leader will combine expertise in executive compensation, global scalability, and digital enablement to create a next-generation total rewards model—anchored in data, automation, and human experience. The role will also build the structures, systems, and shared-service capabilities needed to scale efficiently while maintaining governance, equity, and agility.

The location is flexible across Genmab’s global hubs (Princeton, Copenhagen, Utrecht). We have a hybrid model that requires being onsite 60% of the time.

**Responsibilities

****Strategic Design & Operating Model

**

• Define and lead the evolution of Genmab’s total rewards philosophy and structure to support a global, end-to-end biotech organization.

• Design a modern total rewards operating model that integrates regional teams, shared services, and centers of excellence for consistent global delivery.

• Drive process standardization and automation to improve quality, transparency, and efficiency.

• Lead a strategic compensation team responsible for developing forward-looking frameworks, tools, and analytics that enable proactive support to HR Business Partners, Talent, and other COE stakeholders.

• Ensure the Total Rewards function continuously evolves its offerings to meet the changing needs of a high-growth, science-driven organization.

**Executive Compensation & Governance

**

• Serve as lead advisor to the Board’s Remuneration Committee on executive and equity compensation.

• Design performance-based and ESG-linked long-term incentive plans aligned with Genmab’s business strategy and culture.

• Ensure strong governance, compliance, and transparency in all executive pay matters.

• Bring external perspective and best-in-class practices to inform committee discussions and program evolution, ensuring Genmab remains competitive within the biotech and broader life sciences markets.

**Global Rewards Strategy & Wellbeing

**

• Oversee global compensation, benefits, recognition, and mobility programs that balance competitiveness, scalability, and inclusivity.

• Integrate skills-based pay, internal mobility, and evolving career architectures into the total rewards framework.

• Evolve wellbeing and flexibility offerings through technology and personalized employee experiences.

• Champion employee understanding and appreciation of Total Rewards by partnering with Communications and HR to create clear, engaging messaging that connects programs to our purpose, values, and “EVP”.

• Regularly assess market trends, benchmark data, and emerging innovations to identify opportunities for differentiation and continuous improvement.

**Technology, Automation & Data

**

• Lead implementation of digital total rewards platforms and process automation across compensation, benefits, and equity administration.

• Establish robust analytics capabilities for pay equity, retention risk, and predictive modeling.

• Drive continuous improvement through data insights, benchmarking, and feedback loops.

• Leverage advanced analytics to generate actionable insights for business leaders, enabling data-driven decisions around talent retention, productivity, and performance outcomes.

**Governance & Continuous Improvement

**

• Strengthen global governance structures and ensure alignment with regulatory, financial, and ethical standards.

• Create transparency and consistency through standardized processes, policies, and data.

• Build and mentor a global total rewards team with strong analytical and design skills.

**Requirements

**

• 15+ years of experience in total rewards, with significant leadership in global, complex organizations.

• Deep expertise in executive compensation design, governance, and disclosure.

• Proven success implementing technology, analytics, and automation within HR or total rewards functions.

• Experience designing shared-service or center of excellence models across geographies.

• Strong understanding of compensation and benefits regulations across multiple markets.

• Exceptional ability to influence and communicate at the executive and Board level.

• Demonstrated success leading and developing global teams, fostering capability growth and functional excellence.

• Proven ability to translate external best practices and market intelligence into actionable strategies tailored to the biotech industry.

**Attributes

**

• Visionary leader who designs systems for long-term scalability.

• Digital innovator who applies automation and analytics to improve the employee experience.

• Trusted advisor who balances strategic foresight with operational excellence.

• Inclusive, globally minded leader who champions fairness and sustainability in rewards.

**The Role

**The Senior Manager, Biostatistics acts as a biostatistician supporting the clinical development of compounds as compound lead, primarily up until proof of concept, and/or as trial responsible statistician.

**Responsibilities

**Compound/Indication Level

• Act as lead and main point of contact related to Statistics for designated compound/indication

• Follow scientific and technical progress within the field of biostatistics in drug development and advise of new methodologies that may support innovation and improve efficiencies

• Engage with regulatory authorities on compound/indication level discussions

• Acts as a role model

• Ensures consistency of statistical methods and data handling across trials

• Ensures all compound/indication related work and information is shared between biostatisticians involved in the compound and with the vendor

• Supports compound responsible programmer in developing an integrated database specification

**CDT Member

**

• Responsible for giving statistical input to overall strategy and the synopsis development in the CDT

• Provide scientific advice to the CDT including design of trials, analyses and analyses requiring advanced statistical methodologies/techniques

• Represent the CDT/the company at regulatory meetings, during Key Opinion Leaders meetings, network and/or Partner meetings, as applicable

• Drive design and synopsis development together with relevant stakeholders

• Ensure transparent communication to relevant stakeholders from the CDT

• Ensure availability of integrated database(s), as needed, and planning and conduct of integrated analysis to support development decisions, submissions, and marketing needs

• Support development and communication in relation to communication strategy and/or scientific input to presentations, posters, and articles

Trial Level

• Represent Genmab during meetings/congresses and courses and perform professional networking

• Engage with regulatory authorities on trial level discussions

• Arranges/attends lessons learned to share learnings

• Represents Genmab during Key Opinion Leaders meetings

• Ensure biostatistician review of partner synopsis, protocols, statistical analysis plans, results meetings presentations and clinical trial reports

• Coordinate data transfers from/to business partners in collaboration with the programmer and the data manager, as applicable

**CTT Member

**

• Participate and represent Biostatistics

• Review and provide input to protocol and amendment development

• Perform vendor oversight according to applicable SOPs

• Give input to eCRF setup, edit checks, validation plan, protocol deviations classifications, DSUR, IB updates, tables, figures, and listings etc.

• Review assay validation reports, as applicable

• Perform exploratory analysis, ad hoc analyses, and modelling of data

• Review and approve randomization and stratification plans

• Perform UAT of Randomization part of the IRT system as applicable

• Ensure procedures for blinding are in place as applicable

• Support timely delivery of statistical deliverables

• Responsible for planning and conducting trial result meetings

• Review and approve the CSR

• Attend operational and steering committee meetings, as applicable

• Support regulatory submission/filing activities

**Requirements

**

• MS / PhD or equivalent in a statistical discipline

• 5+ years of experience in relevant area preferred or demonstrated capability

• Experience in statistical analysis, modelling and simulation and adaptive trial designs

• Experience in working with clinical trials

• Preferred experience with oncology clinical trials

• Proficient programming skills in statistical software’s, such as SAS

• Excellent oral and written communication skills

• Ability to work independently as well as in teams

• Confident, self-reliant, and a quick learner

• Proactive and open-minded

• Ability to prioritize and work in a fast-paced and changing environment

• Result and goal-oriented and committed to contributing to the overall success of Genmab
